title: Continuous output segmentation and reconnect resilience for SSE streams
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: implement a resilient Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming layer that: 1) emits strongly delimited, idempotent chunks so clients can safely resume after disconnects; 2) aligns chunk boundaries with structured outputs and function/tool-calling tokens; and 3) provides deterministic resume semantics that are backward-compatible with our existing event-stream clients and OpenAI-style consumers.

Scope and constraints: We must not require changes from the majority of SDK users. The solution should minimize extra metadata per chunk, keep latency low for single-message streams, and work with KV-cache / prefix-caching assumptions in the runtime. We need a graceful strategy for mixed payloads (raw text streaming, JSON-structured blocks, and tool invocations) so partial chunks don't produce invalid structured output when resumed.

Proposed approach:
- Chunking: emit each SSE event with a compact envelope: event: token_chunk; data: <base64 or utf8 payload>; id: <monotonic_chunk_id>; seq: <session_seq>; boundary: <type tag e.g. "detached_json_start" | "detached_json_end" | "plain">. The chunk_id is globally monotonic per-session; seq increments per message batch.
- Idempotency: store last-acked chunk_id in client-visible resume_token header when stream ends or periodically via a heartbeat event. On reconnect, client provides resume_token; server replays any unacked chunks or returns resume_ok with the next expected chunk_id.
- Semantic boundaries: runtime should mark chunks that contain the start/end of structured objects (function call JSON, system delimiter blocks). This prevents reassembly ambiguity on resume. If the stream resumes mid-JSON, server will send a small rehydration prefix event containing the minimal deterministic state required to reconstruct the parser state (e.g., open-brace depth, partial key name) rather than resending the entire context which is expensive.
- Compatibility: default mode uses OpenAI-compatible event names ("event: message", "event: done") for existing clients. Advanced envelope fields are opt-in via a query param or header (X-RI-Stream-Mode: strict-resume). Older clients will still get readable text chunks and a final "done" event.
- Backpressure and batching: continuous small tokens are coalesced by heuristic within a 5ms window to avoid high small-payload overhead. For low-latency single token cases, coalescing can be disabled per-route.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reconnect tests simulate mid-chunk disconnect and validate resumed output is byte-for-byte equal to original logical message reassembly.
- Structured output tests ensure JSON function-call payloads are never observed in a corrupted state by SDK parsers after resume.
- Latency regression vs current streaming must be < 3ms P50 on typical prompts.
- Back-compat: existing SDKs that do not send resume_token recover to the last safe checkpoint without duplicate function calls or truncated JSON.

Risks and trade-offs: providing richer resume metadata increases bandwidth slightly but dramatically reduces ambiguous reassembly. The rehydration-prefix approach trades off some implementation complexity in the runtime parser; however it avoids re-sending entire prefix contexts which would be costly for long-lived conversations.

Docs and UX work: add SDK examples for resume_token usage, header controls for strict-resume mode, and a troubleshooting page on common resume failure modes.
updates: 2025-11-06: Spike completed — implemented prototype that tags JSON boundaries and records chunk_id in runtime KV. Found edge-case when function-call JSON spans > 16KB causing client JSON parser to throw; agreed to add explicit boundary events for 'structured_chunk_continue'.

2025-11-08: Design review with Platform and SDK teams. SDKs requested a single boolean flag for strict resume rather than new header variants. Decided to support X-RI-Stream-Mode with values 'compat'|'strict' for now; SDKs to add sugar wrapper in next release.

2025-11-11: Security review triage — no secrets in event envelopes; resume tokens are opaque HMACs tied to session and TTL=5m. Logging plan approved. Added mandatory rate limiter for resume attempts to mitigate abuse.

2025-11-14: Integration tests added (reconnect mid-json, reconnect after done, rapid connect/disconnect burst). Two tests failing intermittently — root cause: race between checkpoint flush and KV cache eviction. Mitigating fix landed in ENG-47102 and rebase scheduled.

2025-11-18: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482 — implements envelope, heartbeat event, and compatibility fallbacks. Seeking review from @marie-ops on observability hooks and @samir-sdk on client ergonomics.
comments: Diego Morales: Dropped initial prototype into staging. Need SDK change to surface resume_token to users. Moving to In Progress — blocking: SDK wrapper and KV eviction fix.
Marie Ops: Please ensure every resume path emits a trace id for debugging. Also add a metric for 'resume_success_rate' and 'resume_duplicate_count'.
Samir Patel (SDK): We'll add a high-level Stream.resume() that accepts resume_token and hides header plumbing. We prefer the boolean helper over raw header manipulation for most languages.
QA: Suggest adding fuzz tests that chop SSE frames at arbitrary byte offsets to validate reassembly correctness across languages.
